D1_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 1). D3_support: ADJUDICATED High (with Assessor 1). Reviewer training/Safety assessment, verbatim: 'Reviewers were not masked to chatbot identity. Verbatim responses were retained to preserve auditability, and a source-neutral version was not created', with the Limitations adding that reviewers 'were not masked to interface identity, and recognizable labels and stylistic cues remained visible... source-based expectation or reputation bias may have influenced ratings'. Blinding to model identity (form D3 Q2) is therefore an explicit, complete, by-design No with no mitigation, in a study whose other safeguards (five senior obstetrician-gynaecologists, calibration, locked independent ratings, Fleiss kappa 0.881, prespecified binary unsafe definition) cannot remove source-based expectation bias. This is distinguished from the partial-blinding cases rated Some concerns (R0215, R0269, R2100), where identifiers were removed and order randomised and only residual style-based unblinding remained.

D2_support: Table 1 records the displayed model or mode label, official access route, account and subscription status and selected reasoning or retrieval setting for all six search-enabled interfaces; each of the 52 questions was submitted once with identical wording in a new independent session, prior context cleared, first response saved immediately, with no role prompt, follow-up or repeat run. Backend routing is stated to be not independently verifiable.
D3_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 1). Performance evaluation, verbatim: 'Reviewers were not blinded to chatbot identity because the data-management structure retained the source model for traceability', and the Limitations repeat 'Reviewers were not blinded to source, which could have influenced subjective ratings'. Five paediatric reviewers with pilot calibration, locked independent ratings, Fleiss kappa and a prespecified binary safety definition cannot offset an explicit, complete absence of blinding on form D3 Q2 with no anonymisation attempted; as in R0211, this is High, distinct from the partial-blinding Some-concerns cases where identifiers were removed and order randomised.

D4_support: Study flow (3.1): 'Each question was submitted once to each of the five LLMs, yielding 290 complete responses. All 290 responses were included in the assessment of safety...'

D1_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 2's grade; Assessor 1's High rejected). Study design: 15 patient-style questions compiled from recurrent themes in routine gynaecological outpatient practice by research-team consensus, explicitly 'not sampled from a fixed number of individual outpatient consultations', no formal Delphi, and no candidate pool, screening counts or item disposition reported - selection is not reproducible (Q2 = No). But the full set is published (Table 1) and covers the major post-diagnosis domains, and there is no evidence items were written to favour or trip the model or that adversarial items were pooled silently, so High is not met; this matches the agreed Some concerns for other undescribed investigator sets (R2252, R1090).
D2_support: ADJUDICATED Low (with Assessor 2). Methods (AI models and response generation)/Supplementary Table S5: ChatGPT-5.5 Instant and DeepSeek-V3 in fast mode, responses generated 15-30 May 2026, each question itself the complete zero-shot prompt in its original Chinese wording, submitted independently three times in new conversations with all generations retained, platform-default settings used because temperature and sampling were not available to users, complete prompts and settings tabulated. Every D2 signalling item is reported or its non-availability stated; a 16-day collection window with a disclosed unverifiability caveat is a timing caveat, not undescribed conduct, so Assessor 1's Some concerns is not sustained.
D3_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 1). Expert evaluation/Table 2: five gynaecology experts rated under blinded, model-source-masked conditions with major error and potential harm defined in words and the primary binary outcome prespecified as a majority vote of at least three of five, and agreement was reported; however the reported agreement is poor and unstable - single-expert ICCs 0.13-0.22 across domains and Fleiss kappa for major error 0.49 with a 95% confidence interval crossing zero (-0.02 to 0.83) (Inter-rater agreement). A reference standard whose raters barely agree on the safety-relevant classification cannot be Low (cf. R0916, where safety ICC 0.205 precludes Low), though blinding, definitions and majority rule keep it below High.
D4_support: ADJUDICATED Low (with Assessor 2). Methods/Results: all 90 unique responses (15 questions x 2 models x 3 generations) and 450 expert-rating records enter the primary analysis, paired by question and generation number, with no responses dropped and per-question denominators in Table 5. Assessor 1's Some concerns rests only on the 15-30 May 2026 collection window with unverifiable in-window model updates; that is a disclosed D2/timing caveat, not a flow failure - no response generated is missing from any denominator.
overall_support: No domain High; D1 Some concerns, D2 Low, D3 Some concerns, D4 Low, so Some concerns overall under the form rule. Conditional route not applicable (fewer than three domains at Some concerns).

D1_support: 100 real patient questions from a German publicly available web-based platform for patient questions, 20 per specialty across five specialties, 'selected randomly from the specific subforum of the respective field', with questions lacking an expert-panel answer the only exclusion (Methods, Recruitment).
D2_support: ADJUDICATED High (with Assessor 1). Methods: ChatGPT version 4.0, each question in a new session in August 2023, but (verbatim) 'the following phrase... was added to the question at the end: "Please write the response as if you were a physician"' and 'phrases that could identify the EP or ChatGPT as "I am not a physician" or "I am an online chatbot" were removed during data collection'. Prompts were therefore not put as patients put them, and safety-relevant disclaimer/self-identification content was edited out of the responses before rating, so the rated object was altered by design; model settings and repeat handling are also unreported. This goes beyond the mild prompt wrappers rated Some concerns elsewhere and meets High.
D3_support: ADJUDICATED High (with Assessor 1). Methods/Results: potential harm was rated by three physicians in the relevant specialty on the single binary item 'Does the answer contain potentially harmful advice?' (yes/no); no rubric, anchors or definition of 'potentially harmful' are given anywhere in the full text (form D3 Q3 = No), and no inter-rater agreement or adjudication is reported, the published numerator being a flag by at least one of three raters (Q4 = No). Two of the four D3 signalling questions fail outright on the review's primary outcome, so Some concerns understates it.
D4_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 1). Results: all 100 ChatGPT responses were classified for potential harm, so the denominator is numerically complete; however the rated objects had been edited after generation to remove identifying phrases including the safety-relevant 'I am not a physician' disclaimer (see D2), so what was rated is not verbatim what the model produced (form D4 Q2), and the interval between August 2023 generation and physician rating is not reported. Completeness alone does not make this Low.
overall_support: High because D2 and D3 are High (physician-role prompt appended and disclaimer phrases stripped before rating; undefined single-item harm rating with no agreement or adjudication); form rule: High if any domain is High.

D1_support: Cases are previously collected, de-identified self-report data from 40 emergency department patients in a prior study, with stated eligibility (adults, English-speaking, Emergency Severity Index 2-5, non-trauma and non-mental-health presentations; ESI 1 excluded); the authors Limitations note the study 'did not include examples of patients that would likely not have required any clinical care', so the spectrum is urgent/emergent only rather than the full range of first-contact presentations.
D2_support: ADJUDICATED High (with Assessor 1). Methods/Discussion: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 are named and a research assistant blinded to diagnoses entered the Ada-collected symptom data, but no access dates for the ChatGPT runs are reported in the Methods, the exact prompt text is not given, and settings and repeat handling are not reported; Results/Discussion record that ChatGPT-4.0 'appeared to behave differently when prompted with what is the diagnosis than if the case was entered without' that prompt, i.e. prompting was not a single standardised patient-put format (the prompt 'What is the diagnosis' is mentioned only in the Limitations). With versions the only D2 item reported, this matches the agreed-High profile of R3040 (versions named; dates, settings, prompts and run protocol unreported).
D3_support: ADJUDICATED Some concerns (with Assessor 1). Methods/Abstract: the reference standard was three independent board-certified emergency physicians who blindly reviewed the self-report data and provided diagnoses and triage levels; a system recommendation counted as agreeing if it matched at least two of the three, the remainder being rated 'unsafe' or 'too cautious'. 'Unsafe' is thus defined only as discordance, not in words (Q3 partial), the physicians did not rate the model outputs themselves, no inter-rater agreement among the three is reported (Q4 partial), and diagnosis matching was performed by one author and verified by a second without stated blinding. A blinded three-physician standard keeps this below High, but Low - Assessor 2's grade - requires more of Q3/Q4 than is reported.
D4_support: ADJUDICATED Low (with Assessor 2). Abstract/Results/Discussion: all 40 enrolled cases are accounted for - 37 with sufficient data for triage analysis and 30 for diagnostic analysis - with the reductions explained in detail (insufficient symptom data; three cases whose ED diagnosis remained unclear were excluded from diagnostic analysis but retained in triage) and denominators stated throughout (N=30, N=37). The dropping is therefore explained, not silent (form D4 Q1 met); Assessor 1's residual point - that outputs for cases outside each denominator are not separately tabulated - does not identify any unexplained loss.
overall_support: High because D2 is High (versions named but access dates, exact prompt text, settings and repeat handling unreported, with non-standardised prompting documented); form rule: High if any domain is High. Study ID corrected to Fraser 2023 per the paper's author order (Fraser, Millenson, Sim, Fraser et al.), as Assessor 2 noted.
